## 1. Introduction

This report explores the music dataset provided by an online streaming company. The goal is to understand the data quality, find patterns, and help data analysts collect better data in the future.

## 2. Data Import and Setup

First, we will load the necessary libraries and the dataset.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required libraries for analysis
library(tidyverse)   # For data manipulation and plotting
library(ggplot2)     # For graphs
library(dplyr)       # For data wrangling
library(corrplot)    # For correlation heatmaps
library(readr)       # For reading CSV files

# Loading the datasets
data <- read_csv("data.csv")

# Show first few rows
head(data)

# Show dimensions(rows x columns)
cat("Dataset dimensions:", dim(data)[1], "rows and", dim(data)[2], "columns\n\n")

# Show data types
str(data)

# Select only required columns
required_features <- c("acousticness", "artists", "danceability", "energy", 
                       "id", "liveness", "loudness", "name", "popularity", 
                       "speechiness", "tempo", "valence")

data_clean <- data %>% select(all_of(required_features))

# Check for the missing values
missing_values <- sum(is.na(data_clean))
cat("Total missing values in selected features:", missing_values, "\n")

# Remove the duplicates
data_clean <- data_clean %>% distinct()
cat("After removing duplicates:", nrow(data_clean), "rows remain\n")

# Check data types
sapply(data_clean, class)

# Summary of numeric columns
summary(data_clean %>% select_if(is.numeric))

top_artists <- data_clean %>% 
  count(artists) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% 
  head(10)

top_artists

ggplot(data_clean, aes(x = popularity)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Song Popularity", 
       x = "Popularity", 
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

data_clean %>% 
  mutate(energy_group = cut(energy, breaks = 4, 
                            labels = c("Low", "Medium-Low", "Medium-High", "High"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = energy_group, y = popularity)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "orange") +
  labs(title = "Popularity vs. Energy Level",
       x = "Energy Group",
       y = "Popularity") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data_clean, aes(x = danceability, y = valence)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "purple", size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Danceability vs. Valence",
       x = "Danceability",
       y = "Valence") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(top_artists, aes(x = reorder(artists, n), y = n)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "darkgreen") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Artists by Number of Tracks",
       x = "Artist",
       y = "Number of Tracks") +
  theme_minimal()

# Select only numeric columns for correlation
numeric_data <- data_clean %>% select_if(is.numeric)
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Create correlation heatmap
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         tl.cex = 0.7,
         title = "Correlation Between Music Features",
         mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))

# Relationship between popularity and danceability
ggplot(data_clean, aes(x = danceability, y = popularity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Popularity vs Danceability",
       x = "Danceability",
       y = "Popularity") +
  theme_minimal()

```
